title: Hello, C++
bridge: C++ programs start in `int main()`, and `std::cout << ... ;` prints. `<<` chains pieces together and `"\n"` ends a line. Statements end with `;`, blocks use `{ }`. Unlike Python, the whole file is compiled first, so one typo stops everything.

exercises.title: Hello from C++
Fix it (compiler drill)
exercises.prompt:
Three mistakes stop this compiling. Fix them until it prints:
C++ is strict
and that helps
10
hints: Read the first error: which line, and what did it expect?
A missing ;, a missing std::, and a missing closing quote.

quiz.q: Where does a C++ program start?

quiz.why: Each piece is printed straight after the last.

quiz.q: There are 12 errors. Which do you fix first?
quiz.why: Later errors are often caused by the first one.
